author: akmaurya
wrong: The tier-1 analysis router (analysis_tier1) classified most Run4 subtracted SAXS curves as WAXS or SWAXS based on detected 'sharp peaks' in the high-q tail.
right: None of the Run4 measurements contain real WAXS/Bragg peaks (operator-confirmed). Treat all Run4 curves as pure SAXS; ignore/discount any Bragg-peak detection on Run4 data and do not truncate the Guinier/power-law/Porod windows at a detected 'peak' q for this series.

author: akmaurya
wrong: When query_manifest(query_type='files'/'averaged', ...) returns a truncated file list (e.g. "Showing 15 of 23 matches"), concluding a stage (e.g. 'subtracted') is absent just because no matching filename is visible in that truncated list.
right: Always read the `by_stage` / `by_detector` summary counts in the SAME response FIRST and treat them as ground truth (e.g. "subtracted": 1 means one subtracted file exists, full stop). Only scan the file list for names/details once existence is confirmed by the counts. If the list is truncated and a specific file is needed, re-query with a narrower keyword instead of eyeballing a partial list or declaring the stage missing. Never tell the user a file/stage is missing without first checking the summary counts.
